resources.string: Detects when a YouTube Short, TikTok or Instagram Reel is on screen and reads its title and creator, so the audio check knows when to listen. When you tap ✱, the title and creator are sent to the ShortCheck server. In other apps it reads only which app is in front (its package name), to stop listening when you leave. No screenshots.
Before you turn on the ShortCheck service

ShortCheck uses Android's Accessibility service to see when a reel is playing. It is not an accessibility tool.

What it reads:
• In YouTube, TikTok and Instagram: the title or caption and the creator of the reel on screen.
• In any other app: only which app is in front (its package name), so it can stop listening when you leave. Nothing else on screen.

What leaves your phone:
• Once you have watched a reel for 5 seconds (with audio check on): its audio, sent to the ShortCheck server, which has it transcribed by a third-party speech-to-text provider (Google Gemini by default).
• When you tap ✱: the reel's title and creator, sent to the ShortCheck server to identify and fact-check the video.

Why: so ShortCheck can fact-check the reel you are watching when you ask it to. Audio from reels you swipe past in under 5 seconds never leaves the phone. The server does not save audio and drops transcripts after 10 minutes.

You can turn the service off at any time in Settings → Accessibility.
